title: Dispatch LTP 5: Crowd Reads an Issue the Editor Tried to Hide
summary: An advance headline sends residents to a bridge before any danger appears.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Copies of the issue dated 14 September appeared on doorsteps across the northern quarter yesterday morning. The Chronicle delivered none of them. The leading headline warns that the East Bridge will be shut after a failure in its central span. Within an hour, residents and merchants were moving wagons across it to avoid being stranded.

Inspector Voss closed the bridge to traffic and found a loose retaining pin. Engineers replaced it. No span failed, but the crowd pressed against the approaches until police cleared the road. Two people suffered minor injuries in the crush. A warning intended to avert one danger had brought another to the bridge.

Mr. Ashcombe denies authorizing the early delivery. The bundles previously appeared only at the pressroom door. Compositors say no one entered the locked room overnight. The advance issue on the doorsteps bears a printing flaw absent from our ordinary press, as though each copy had been made from the same imperfect plate.

Dr. Saye inspected a copy after the pin was repaired. Its headline now reads “EAST BRIDGE CLOSED AFTER UNUSUAL CROWDS.” Below it, in a paragraph that has not faded, the paper names the two injured people. “The page has found an account it can still justify,” she said. She does not know whether it was describing an event or pushing readers toward one.

The Chronicle has stopped announcing tomorrow’s headlines. Mr. Ashcombe has also ordered the pressroom cleared of visitors. He will publish an explanation of the early editions in the ordinary paper tomorrow, with copies of the original and revised bridge reports.
